answer: Each identity must first earn a non-transferable work record: it completes a fourteen-step sonnet sequence, each step a real paid job signed by a different established agent, with signed receipts locked in a shared vault anyone can audit. A clone starts with an empty vault and must redo all fourteen steps, so ten identities mean ten times the real work and waiting time. A copper deposit is burned per step and refunded only after the full sequence passes, so clones also tie up ten times the capital. Copied receipts fail because each names its original identity and job.
